claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Under vertex deletion and edge contraction, the inverse image of each surviving target vertex is a nonempty connected branch set. Two branch sets are adjacent exactly when the corresponding target vertices are adjacent, since edge deletion is unavailable. This gives precisely the stated model, and contracting any such model gives K6 minus an edge. Seven labels enumerate every model; all connectivity and adjacency conditions are checkable in O(n²), proving NP membership and the stated O(7^n n²) bound.
claims.search_method: Definition-level branch-set proof, supplemented by an exact integer-bit-mask implementation of the certificate predicate.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: A complete graph has no anticomplete nonempty branch-set pair. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, the endpoints of any nonedge together with those four vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices, while every other vertex is among the at most 2q endpoints of the q nonedges, so n≤2q+3. Applying Claim 0 gives the runtime. If q≤c log n for fixed c, its exponential factor is polynomial in n.
claims.search_method: Complete combinatorial case split plus exhaustive exact enumeration of every labeled graph on at most seven vertices.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: The t−2 core branch sets give t−2 internally disjoint routes between the two exceptional branch sets, so every separator disjoint from them has size at least t−2. An inclusion-minimal such separator S is a clique in a chordal graph and both exceptional-side components are full to S. In any full component, choosing a vertex with maximum S-neighborhood and applying chordality along a shortest path to any missed s∈S proves that some vertex is complete to S. Taking one such vertex from each side and any t−2 vertices of S induces exactly Kt minus the edge between the two side vertices. The converse is immediate. Enumeration gives O(n^6) for t=6.
claims.search_method: Independent minimal-separator proof and exhaustive counterexample search over all chordal labeled graphs on at most seven vertices.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Anticompleteness forces both exceptional branch sets into one part, where connectivity forces each to be a singleton. A core branch is either a singleton in a distinct outside part or spans at least two parts and can be reduced to a cross-part edge without losing any required adjacency. Hence the remaining nonsingleton cores are exactly a matching after reserving the exceptional and singleton-core vertices. In a complete multipartite graph every matching is bounded by ⌊M/2⌋ and M−L, and pairing vertices from different largest remaining parts attains their minimum. The criterion is therefore necessary and sufficient.
claims.search_method: Structural necessity-and-sufficiency proof plus independent exact branch-set enumeration for all 138 complete-multipartite isomorphism types on at most ten vertices.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: The proposed nice-decomposition state records exactly the information needed: bag labels, the connectivity partition within every branch label, whether each label is unseen/active/closed, and the fourteen required-adjacency bits. Once a component loses its last bag vertex, separator locality makes future reconnection impossible, justifying the closure rule. Compatible join states combine partitions by transitive closure and reject disconnected duplicate closed copies. There are 7^(w+1) labelings and at most Bell(w+1) compatible combined partitions, with only constant additional status and adjacency data; even quadratic join processing remains 2^{O(w log w)} per bag.
claims.search_method: Direct dynamic-program invariant, transition, acceptance-condition, and state-count audit.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two four-vertex paths and four singleton c-vertices form the displayed model. A singleton exceptional branch needs four distinct neighbors, excluding every path vertex and forcing it to be some ci. Its anticomplete exceptional mate must be an interval in a component of A−ai or B−bi. For i=2 or 3 every such interval has at most three external neighbors. For i=1 or 4, the only intervals with four external neighbors force one core branch to contain the isolated endpoint a1, a4, b1, or b4 after deleting the exceptional pair; that core is then a singleton anticomplete to the other cores. Exact exhaustive search confirmed that no singleton-exceptional model exists.
claims.witness: The graph has path edges a1a2,a2a3,a3a4 and b1b2,b2b3,b3b4; all six edges among c1,c2,c3,c4; spokes aici and bici for i=1,2,3,4; and no other edges. Its valid model is ({a1,a2,a3,a4},{b1,b2,b3,b4},{c1},{c2},{c3},{c4}).
claims.search_method: Degree and external-neighborhood analysis plus exact enumeration of all connected branch subsets; all 40 feasible connected anticomplete ordered exceptional pairs with a singleton endpoint were checked.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for the unrestricted complexity classification and, if tractable, a polynomial-time detection algorithm. The draft explicitly states that it does not resolve the unrestricted P-versus-NP-complete question and supplies neither an unrestricted polynomial algorithm nor a hardness classification. Its verified certificate, parameterized algorithm, restricted-class algorithms, and normalization obstruction are material progress but do not cover the requested target at full strength. Thus VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is accurate rather than overstated or understated; its final writeup also does not claim full coverage.
